newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RAINBOW CHICKEN GUTTED BY PROFIT WARNING.
newsitem.headline: RAINBOW CHICKEN GUTTED BY PROFIT WARNING.

text.p: Shares in Rainbow Chicken Ltd slumped 16 percent to a fresh year low of 65 cents after the struggling broiler producer warned yet again of big losses.
The company said in a statement earlier that it would report losses significantly higher than expected in the half-year to September.
"The announcement was unexpected. The reality of these losses have been around for some time but obviously people panic when they see the announcement and they sell it down," a trader said.
The dealer added that he expected the counter to recover slightly, possibly back up to the 77 cent level it started the day at.
By the close of trade at 1400 GMT, the counter had slipped further to 60 cents -- a 17 cent or 22 percent loss on the day.
The company has issued a string of profit warnings over the last year, after being hit by rising feed costs and fierce competition.

In November last year, it appointed Jorge Antonio Del Corral Ibarrondo, the former head of a Mexico's largest broiler and egg producer, as its new chief executive as part of a plan to haul the company out of the red.
Analysts had been hoping the company would pare its losses on the back of more stable costs and better domestic chicken prices.
